title: How Texas Banned Almost All Abortions

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我负责报道《纽约时报》每日简讯 DealBook 的商业与政策新闻，

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些举足轻重的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily today.
sentences.zh: 这是今日头条。

sentences.en: A Texas law banning most abortions has gone into effect with the blessing of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 在最高法院的默许下，一项禁止绝大多数堕胎的德克萨斯州法律已经正式生效。

sentences.en: I spoke with my colleague, Adam Liptack, about why this law survived a legal process that so many previous anti-abortion laws have not.
sentences.zh: 我和我的同事亚当·利普塔克聊了聊，探讨为什么这项法律能够在一项又一项以往的反堕胎法折戟沉沙的法律程序中幸存下来。

sentences.en: It's Friday, September 3rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月3日，星期五。

sentences.en: Adam, pretty much since the start of this show, at the beginning of the Trump administration, we have been talking with you about this moment when
sentences.zh: 亚当，几乎从本节目开播起，即特朗普政府上台之初，我们就一直在跟你讨论这样一个时刻：

sentences.en: the increasingly conservative Supreme Court might take direct aim at abortion rights and Roe v.
sentences.zh: 日益保守的最高法院可能会直接将矛头指向堕胎权以及“罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: Wade.

sentences.en: And you had warned us that the court would be slow to do that, to avoid the perception of being too political.
sentences.zh: 而你曾警告我们，法院行动会比较迟缓，以避免给人留下过于政治化的印象。

sentences.en: And now we have this ruling.
sentences.zh: 现在我们迎来了这项裁决。

sentences.en: So is this that big moment?
sentences.zh: 那么，这就是那个重大时刻吗？

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 算是也不是。

sentences.en: I mean, what the court has accomplished is in Texas, women now, as a practical matter, can't get abortions after six weeks.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法院在德克萨斯州取得的成果是，从实际操作来看，女性现在在怀孕六周后就无法堕胎了。

sentences.en: That's blatantly at odds with Roe, which says that before viability, which is to say about 22 to 24 weeks, states can't ban abortion.
sentences.zh: 这公然与“罗诉韦德案”相悖，该案规定，在胎儿具有独立生存能力之前（大约是22到24周），各州不得禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: So in that sense, this is completely at odds with Roe.
sentences.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，这完全违背了“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: At the same time, it was, the majority would say, a modest procedural ruling, not definitive.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，多数派会说，这是一个温和的程序性裁决，并非最终定论。

sentences.en: They didn't decide to overrule Roe.
sentences.zh: 他们没有决定推翻“罗诉韦德案”。

sentences.en: They didn't decide a constitutional question at all, they say.
sentences.zh: 他们表示，根本没有对宪法问题作出裁决。

sentences.en: But this decision, just before midnight on Wednesday, as a practical matter,
sentences.zh: 但这项在周三午夜之前作出的决定，从实际效果来看，

sentences.en: overturned the ability of women in Texas to get the abortions that Roe guarantees them.
sentences.zh: 剥夺了德克萨斯州女性获得“罗诉韦德案”所保障的堕胎服务的权利。

sentences.en: Well, like you said, it is that moment and it's not that moment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如你所说，这既是那个时刻，又不是那个时刻。

sentences.en: And I want to get to all that.
sentences.zh: 我想深入探讨所有这些问题。

sentences.en: But
sentences.zh: But

sentences.en: let's talk about how this case ended up at the Supreme Court in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这个案件最初是如何闹到最高法院的。

sentences.en: What should we know about this law and how it came to be?
sentences.zh: 关于这部法律以及它是如何出台的，我们应该了解些什么？

sentences.en: So this Texas law is in a way typical.
sentences.zh: 所以，这部德克萨斯州的法律在某种程度上很有代表性。

sentences.en: Lots of red states have been passing laws that purport to ban abortions after six weeks or 10 weeks or 15 weeks.
sentences.zh: 许多红州一直在通过各种法律，声称要在怀孕六周、十周或十五周后禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: And those are routinely struck down immediately in federal court because they're at odds with Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而这些法律通常会在联邦法院立即被裁定违宪并废止，因为它们与“罗诉韦德案”相冲突。

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: Wade.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: But this law has an innovation.
sentences.zh: 但这部法律有一个创新之处。

sentences.en: It has a special feature that was designed by the legislature to avoid judicial review, to make sure that federal judges can't strike it down.
sentences.zh: 它有一个由立法机构精心设计特殊功能，旨在规避司法审查，确保联邦法官无法将其废止。

sentences.en: And what is that feature?
sentences.zh: 那是什么功能？

sentences.en: That feature, there's two basic pieces to it.
sentences.zh: 那个功能，有两个基本部分。

sentences.en: One is ordinarily, when you want to challenge one of these abortion laws, you sue the government officials in charge of enforcing the law,
sentences.zh: 一是通常情况下，当你想要对其中某项堕胎法提出挑战时，你会起诉负责执行该法律的政府官员，

sentences.en: the governor, the attorney general, people like that.
sentences.zh: 比如州长、总检察长之类的人。

sentences.en: This law says those people have no power to enforce the law.
sentences.zh: 而这部法律规定，这些人没有权力执行该法律。

sentences.en: We specifically exclude them from the enforcement process.
sentences.zh: 我们将他们从执法过程中明确排除在外。

sentences.en: No government official may enforce this law.
sentences.zh: 任何政府官员都不得执行这部法律。

sentences.en: And instead, we deputize every person in the world to file civil lawsuits if they think someone is involved in aiding or abetting or providing an abortion after six weeks.
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，我们授权世界上每一个人，如果他们认为有人参与了协助、教唆或提供怀孕六周后的堕胎服务，就可以提起民事诉讼。

sentences.en: So that's a very novel construct that we're going to deputize, critics would say, vigilantes.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常新颖的架构，批评人士会说，我们这是在授权治安维持会成员（民间 vigilantes）。

sentences.en: And then we're going to incentivize them.
sentences.zh: 然后我们还要激励他们。

sentences.en: They're offered bounties of $10,000 if they sue and win.
sentences.zh: 如果他们起诉并胜诉，将获得1万美元的赏金。

sentences.en: They're offered their attorney's fees if they sue and win.
sentences.zh: 如果他们起诉并胜诉，将获得律师费补偿。

sentences.en: They're allowed to sue in their home county.
sentences.zh: 他们被允许在自己所在的县提起诉讼。

sentences.en: Texas has 254 counties.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州有254个县。

sentences.en: And the abortion provider sued or anyone else who, quote, aids and abets in providing the abortion,
sentences.zh: 被起诉的堕胎提供者，或者任何所谓的“协助和教唆”提供堕胎服务的人，

sentences.en: a counselor, a clergy person, a spouse, an Uber driver, someone who offers to pay for the abortion, all of those people can be sued for at least $10,000 all over Texas.
sentences.zh: 比如咨询师、神职人员、配偶、优步司机、或者出资支付堕胎费用的人，所有这些人都在德克萨斯州各地面临着至少1万美元的诉讼风险。

sentences.en: And not only once.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是一次。

sentences.en: You can have hundreds of people suing over the same act of aiding an abortion in every single county.
sentences.zh: 针对同一起协助堕胎的行为，你可能会在每一个县都面临数百人的起诉。

sentences.en: So anyone who finds out about an abortion being carried out can file a lawsuit out of this law against anyone involved in any way in that abortion.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何发现堕胎行为正在实施的人，都可以根据这项法律对以任何方式参与该堕胎的任何人提起诉讼。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: Wow.

sentences.en: So you kind of terrorize the clinics into stopping providing abortion services, which is happening, because these citizens have all kinds of advantages.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比是通过恐怖手段迫使诊所停止提供堕胎服务，而这正是正在发生的事情，因为这些普通公民享有各种优势。

sentences.en: It's a quite unlevel litigation playing field.
sentences.zh: 这是一个极度不平等的诉讼竞技场。

sentences.en: So the legal analysis of the clinics in Texas is they can't afford to take this risk.
sentences.zh: 因此，德克萨斯州诊所的法律分析是，他们承担不起这个风险。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: Hmm.

sentences.en: So if this law had been written the way most laws seeking to ban abortion are written, it would have specified that government officials enforce it.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这部法律是按照大多数旨在禁止堕胎的法律那样编写的，它就会明确规定由政府官员来执行。

sentences.en: But because the law is written in such a way that those officials are cut out, it therefore kind of circumvents the normal way of objecting to an abortion ban.
sentences.zh: 但由于该法律在编写时将这些官员排除在外，因此它在某种程度上规避了对堕胎禁令提出异议的常规途径。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So abortion providers had a very hard time figuring out who to sue to try to stop the law.
sentences.zh: 因此，堕胎服务提供者很难弄清楚到底该起诉谁来试图阻止这项法律。

sentences.en: Call it creative, call it devious.
sentences.zh: 你可以叫它有创意，也可以叫它诡计多端。

sentences.en: This law is specifically designed to make sure there are no such lawsuits and to make sure that its regime comes into effect, even though it's plainly
sentences.zh: 这部法律的专门设计就是为了确保不会出现此类诉讼，并确保其体制得以生效，尽管它根据现行的最高法院判例，

sentences.en: unconstitutional under prevailing Supreme Court precedents.
sentences.zh: 明显是违宪的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: Mm-hmm.

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So this law is designed to, if it succeeds, just kind of sail through the legal system by bobbing and weaving around all the normal ways that people would legally object to it.
sentences.zh: 所以这部法律的设计目的就是，如果成功的话，通过在所有人们通常对其提出法律异议的常规途径中闪转腾挪，在法律系统中畅通无阻地滑行通过。

sentences.en: Nicely put, yeah.
sentences.zh: 说得好，没错。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: So once this law was signed by the governor of Texas and was set to go into effect, what ends up happening?
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦这部法律被德克萨斯州州长签署并准备生效，最终发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did the authors of this law succeed in making it impossible to figure out who to sue?
sentences.zh: 这部法律的起草者是否成功做到了让人无法弄清该起诉谁？

sentences.en: Well, that depends on which side you believe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这取决于你相信哪一方。

sentences.en: Abortion providers did go to court and they did sue people, among them every judge in the state and every court clerk in the state,
sentences.zh: 堕胎服务提供者确实去了法院并起诉了相关人员，其中包括该州的每一位法官和每一位法院书记员，

sentences.en: on the theory that, well, now they're the people, in fact, who are the government officials in charge of these lawsuits that will be brought by private citizens.
sentences.zh: 其理论依据是，好吧，现在他们实际上才是负责这些将由普通公民提起的诉讼的政府官员。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: Okay.

sentences.en: But the question for the courts at bottom was, had they found proper parties to sue?
sentences.zh: 但对法院来说，最根本的问题是，他们是否找到了适格的被告来起诉？

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: Mm-hmm.

sentences.en: And that's a question that you have to get past before you get to the question of, is it constitutional?
sentences.zh: 这是一个你必须先解决的问题，然后才能讨论它是否违宪。

sentences.en: And the weird thing is, we know it's not constitutional.
sentences.zh: 而奇怪的是，我们都知道它是违宪的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: Mm-hmm.

sentences.en: But we're still hung up on this first question about, of who do you sue?
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然卡在第一个问题上，也就是——你到底该起诉谁？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: So what happens when abortion providers sue all these people you just described, judges, clerks, et cetera?
sentences.zh: 那么，当堕胎服务提供者起诉你刚刚描述的这些人（法官、书记员等）时，发生了什么？

sentences.en: What do the courts say?
sentences.zh: 法院是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Are those the right people?
sentences.zh: 这些人是正确的人选吗？

sentences.en: A federal trial judge says, yes, good enough.
sentences.zh: 一名联邦初审法官表示，是的，足够了。

sentences.en: Those people can be sued.
sentences.zh: 这些人可以被起诉。

sentences.en: And he schedules a hearing about whether to issue a preliminary injunction, whether to halt the law.
sentences.zh: 并且他安排了一场听证会，以决定是否发布初步禁令、是否叫停该法律。

sentences.en: It goes up to an appeals court.
sentences.zh: 案件上诉到了上诉法院。

sentences.en: The appeals court says, wait on, hold on a second.
sentences.zh: 上诉法院说，等等，等一下。

sentences.en: We're going to freeze that hearing.
sentences.zh: 我们要冻结那场听证会。

sentences.en: That hearing can't go forward.
sentences.zh: 听证会不能继续进行。

sentences.en: And so now we have this ticking time bomb where the law is about to come into effect.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了一个即将生效的法律，就像一颗定时炸弹。

sentences.en: And the only option is to go to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 唯一的选择就是上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: And that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发展的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: Unlocked?

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，会怎么样呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅者，今天就下载《时报》App，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So Adam, in what form does this case challenging this creative Texas abortion ban reach the Supreme Court?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，挑战这一极具创意的德克萨斯州堕胎禁令的案件，是以什么形式到达最高法院的？

sentences.en: So abortion providers file an emergency application asking the court to block the law.
sentences.zh: 所以堕胎服务提供者提交了一份紧急申请，请求法院阻止该法律。

sentences.en: These emergency applications, which happen very fast, very thin briefing, no oral argument, are what people who follow the Supreme Court call the shadow docket.
sentences.zh: 这些进展极快、简报非常简短、没有进行口头辩论的紧急申请，被关注最高法院的人士称为“影子 docket（影子 Docket）”。

sentences.en: These are not the usual cases, which take months to decide in oral arguments and full deliberations and elaborate decisions.
sentences.zh: 这些不是通常需要几个月时间通过口头辩论、全面审议和详尽判决来决定的常规案件。

sentences.en: This happens in a matter of days.
sentences.zh: 这件事在几天内就发生了。

sentences.en: And what happens in this case of the shadow docket?
sentences.zh: 在这个影子 docket 的案件中发生了什么？

sentences.en: So the parties file their briefs and we expect a decision from the court before the Texas law goes into effect on September 1St. But we don't get that decision.
sentences.zh: 因此，各方提交了简报，我们原本期望法院在德克萨斯州法律于9月1日生效之前做出裁决。但我们没有得到那个裁决。

sentences.en: We hear nothing from the court and the law comes into effect.
sentences.zh: 我们没有听到法院的任何消息，然后法律就生效了。

sentences.en: About a day after it comes into effect, the court finally issues a decision.
sentences.zh: 在它生效大约一天后，法院终于发布了一项裁决。

sentences.en: It's five to four.
sentences.zh: 票数是五比四。

sentences.en: The majority opinion unsigned, but you can deduce who's in the majority because of the four dissenters.
sentences.zh: 多数派意见没有署名，但你可以通过四位持异议的法官推断出谁属于多数派。

sentences.en: The unsigned majority opinion is only a paragraph long.
sentences.zh: 未署名的多数派意见只有一个段落长。

sentences.en: And it says, listen, we're not deciding the constitutionality of this law, but these are complex procedural questions.
sentences.zh: 它说，听着，我们不是在裁决这项法律的合宪性，但这些都是复杂的程序问题。

sentences.en: It looks like we're not in a position to stop anybody from doing anything because we don't know who the right government official is because there are no government officials.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎无法阻止任何人做任何事，因为我们不知道谁是合适的政府官员，因为根本没有政府官员。

sentences.en: And therefore, the abortion providers haven't made out their case.
sentences.zh: 因此，堕胎服务提供者并没有充分阐明他们的诉求。

sentences.en: And therefore, sorry, but we're going to let this law come into effect.
sentences.zh: 因此，很抱歉，但我们将让这项法律生效。

sentences.en: So the majority basically says that the people who wrote this law kind of cracked the code and figured out how to ban abortion in a way that makes it hard
sentences.zh: 所以多数派基本上是说，写下这部法律的人某种程度上破解了密码，弄清楚了如何以一种让

sentences.en: for us, the Supreme Court justices, to strike down.
sentences.zh: 我们这些最高法院大法官很难推翻的方式来禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: So the authors of this law set out to evade judicial review.
sentences.zh: 因此，这部法律的起草者旨在逃避司法审查。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court majority essentially says, you win.
sentences.zh: 而最高法院的多数派基本上是在说，你们赢了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You did it.
sentences.zh: 你做到了。

sentences.en: And the majority was justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas and the three Trump appointees,
sentences.zh: 投多数票的是塞缪尔·阿利托、克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官，以及特朗普任命的三位法官：

sentences.en: Neil Gorsuch, Brett Kavanaugh, and Amy Coney Barrett.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·戈萨奇、布雷特·卡瓦诺和艾米·科尼·巴雷特。

sentences.en: And I might pause there for a second and note that Barrett makes the difference.
sentences.zh: 我可能会在这里暂停一下，指出巴雷特起到了决定性作用。

sentences.en: Had Ruth Bader Ginsburg been around, she died just last year, this case comes out differently because the 5-4 would have gone the other direction.
sentences.zh: 如果露丝·巴德·金斯伯格还在世的话（她就在去年去世），这个案件的结果就会不同，因为5比4的票数会走向相反的方向。

sentences.en: But just to be clear, these five conservative justices you just identified, they are not endorsing this Texas law.
sentences.zh: 但需要明确的是，你刚提到的这五位保守派大法官，他们并不在为这部德克萨斯州的法律背书。

sentences.en: They're simply saying as written, we just don't really know what to do with it, so we're going to do nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们只是说，按照目前的写法，我们实在不知道该怎么处理它，所以我们什么也不做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: Right.

sentences.en: And they say in so many words, we're not ruling on the constitutionality of the law.
sentences.zh: 他们明确表示，我们不对该法律的合宪性作出裁决。

sentences.en: And we think there may be other settings in which the constitutionality of the law can be decided.
sentences.zh: 并且我们认为，在其他情况下可能会对该法律的合宪性进行裁决。

sentences.en: Like in a state court proceeding, if somebody does sue an abortion provider in Texas under the law, and the provider raises as a defense that the law is unconstitutional,
sentences.zh: 比如在州法院的诉讼程序中，如果有人根据该法律在德克萨斯州起诉了堕胎服务提供者，而提供者以该法律违宪作为抗辩理由，

sentences.en: they suggest that would be a perfectly proper way to decide it.
sentences.zh: 他们暗示这将是裁决此事的完全恰当的方式。

sentences.en: But what we're seeing is that those lawsuits may never happen because the clinics have stopped providing abortions after six weeks.
sentences.zh: 但我们看到的是，这些诉讼可能永远不会发生，因为诊所在怀孕六周后已经停止提供堕胎服务。

sentences.en: So Adam, what about the rest of the justices, the four who dissent?
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，其余四位持异议的大法官情况如何？

sentences.en: What do they say?
sentences.zh: 他们是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Each of them files a separate dissent.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都提交了单独的异议书。

sentences.en: The dissenters are Chief Justice John Roberts and the court's three liberal members, Justices Stephen Breyer, Sonia Sotomayor, and Elena Kagan.
sentences.zh: 持异议者是首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨以及法院的三位自由派成员：斯蒂芬·布雷耶、索尼亚·索托马约尔和埃琳娜·卡根大法官。

sentences.en: And they basically say, wait a minute, it can't be that we're powerless to address this unconstitutional law because someone has come up with a device to block us out.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是说，等一下，我们绝不可能无力应对这项违宪的法律，仅仅是因为有人想出了一个把我们排除在外的花招。

sentences.en: That there must be a way for us to freeze matters at least long enough to give this due consideration and not in a matter of two or three days effectively issue
sentences.zh: 我们一定有一种方法，至少能在足够长的时间内冻结事态，以便对此进行充分审议，而不是在两三天内

sentences.en: such a momentous ruling that changes the abortion landscape in Texas.
sentences.zh: 仓促做出如此重大的裁决，从而改变德克萨斯州的堕胎格局。

sentences.en: What does that mean, freeze matters?
sentences.zh: 这话是什么意思，冻结事态？

sentences.en: And who articulated that concept?
sentences.zh: 是谁提出了这个概念？

sentences.en: All of them make that point in one way or another.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人都以这样或那样的方式提出了这一点。

sentences.en: And they basically say, let's slow down here.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是说，我们慢下来吧。

sentences.en: Let's keep this law on ice until we can have full reasoned deliberation about what should be done with it.
sentences.zh: 把这项法律暂时搁置，直到我们能对如何处理它进行充分、理性的审议。

sentences.en: One of the justices, Justice Sotomayor, really wrote quite directly about what was going on here.
sentences.zh: 其中一位大法官索托马约尔法官，非常直接地写到了这里发生的事情。

sentences.en: She said, the court's order is stunning.
sentences.zh: 她说，法院的命令令人震惊。

sentences.en: Presented with an application to enjoin a flagrantly unconstitutional law engineered to prohibit women from exercising their constitutional rights and evade
sentences.zh: 在面对一项旨在禁止女性行使其宪法权利并逃避

sentences.en: judicial scrutiny, a majority of justices have opted to bury their heads in the sand.
sentences.zh: 司法审查的公然违宪法律的禁令申请时，多数派大法官选择了鸵鸟政策。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So what these justices seem to be saying is, this court should take its time and treat this like
sentences.zh: 所以这些大法官似乎在说，本法院应该花时间，把这当成

sentences.en: any Supreme Court case with oral arguments, judges at the bench, lots of deliberation.
sentences.zh: 任何带有口头辩论、法官在席、大量审议的最高法院案件来处理。

sentences.en: And correct me if I'm wrong, they're saying, in the meantime, until we can do that, this law should not go into effect.
sentences.zh: 如果我没理解错的话，他们的意思是，在此期间，在我们能够这样做之前，这项法律不应生效。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that, in the meantime, is the hard part of the case, because the dissenters are suggesting that they have the power to stop the law from coming into effect.
sentences.zh: 而“在此期间”正是本案最艰难的部分，因为持异议者暗示他们有权阻止法律生效。

sentences.en: And serious legal scholars say, even one sympathetic to the dissenters, you know, larger point of view, say that these are
sentences.zh: 严肃的法律学者表示，甚至是那些同情异议者

sentences.en: difficult questions because the court actually doesn't block or enjoin laws.
sentences.zh: 较大局观的人也说，这些都是棘手的问题，因为法院实际上并不阻止或禁止法律。

sentences.en: It blocks or enjoins people from enforcing laws.
sentences.zh: 它阻止或禁止的是人们执行法律。

sentences.en: And as we've been talking all this time, Michael, the genius or the devil or whatever you want to call it of the Texas law is that it seems to evade that point.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，正如我们一直以来在讨论的那样，德克萨斯州法律的天才之处、魔鬼之处，或者无论你怎么称呼它，在于它似乎避开了这一点。

sentences.en: So there's a legitimate question legally about whether these dissenting justices are correct
sentences.zh: 所以在法律上存在一个合理的问题，即这些持异议的大法官是否正确：

sentences.en: that they and the court have the power to pause this law, prevent it from going into action based on the quirky ways in which it was written.
sentences.zh: 即基于该法律制定的奇特方式，他们和法院是否有权暂停该法律，阻止其实施。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, under existing court doctrine, the majority's point of view has some force.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，在现有的法院教条下，多数派的观点确实有一定道理。

sentences.en: But under, you know, sort of fundamental principles of good government and justice, it just seems very, very odd that a legislature can set out to evade judicial review in order to
sentences.zh: 但在良好政府和正义的某种基本原则下，立法机构为了

sentences.en: do something unconstitutional and succeed because they've been clever.
sentences.zh: 做一些违宪的事情而着手逃避司法审查，并且因为他们很聪明而成功了，这看起来实在是非常非常奇怪。

sentences.en: I mean, you would think the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你会认为

sentences.en: Supreme Court of all institutions would have the power to address that.
sentences.zh: 最高法院作为所有机构中最应该有权力解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So, Adam, since the majority explicitly said we're not ruling on the constitutionality of this Texas abortion ban, what would trigger such a review?
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，既然多数派明确表示我们不对这项德克萨斯州堕胎禁令的合宪性进行裁决，什么样的情况才会触发这样的审查？

sentences.en: Or to put it differently, what recourse is left for abortion right advocates in Texas who want to challenge this law?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，德克萨斯州想要挑战这项法律的堕胎权倡导者还剩下什么救济途径？

sentences.en: So there are two basic routes.
sentences.zh: 所以有两个基本的途径。

sentences.en: One is that the lawsuit in which the Supreme Court ruled is still alive.
sentences.zh: 一是最高法院作出裁决的那起诉讼仍在进行中。

sentences.en: It's at a federal appeals court.
sentences.zh: 它目前在一个联邦上诉法院。

sentences.en: That court will eventually rule and that ruling can be appealed again to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 该法院最终将作出裁决，该裁决可以再次上诉至最高法院。

sentences.en: So that's one route.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一条途径。

sentences.en: Or an abortion provider could decide to offer an abortion to a woman at eight weeks or 10 weeks and take his or her chances, get sued, raise as a defense
sentences.zh: 或者，堕胎服务提供者可以决定为怀孕八周或十周的女性提供堕胎服务，并碰碰运气，遭到起诉，并将

sentences.en: that the Texas law is unconstitutional, probably win, have that case appealed up through the Texas state court system, could reach the Supreme Court directly.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州法律违宪作为辩护理由，大概率会赢，让该案在德克萨斯州州法院系统层层上诉，最终可能直接到达最高法院。

sentences.en: And then you wouldn't have this problem about knowing who to sue and the court could resolve the question on the merits.
sentences.zh: 然后你就不必面对弄清楚该起诉谁的问题了，法院就可以根据案件是非曲直解决这个问题。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And do we expect that to happen?
sentences.zh: 我们预计会发生这种情况吗？

sentences.en: It seems that clinics are abiding by the law, that clinics don't want to take the risk that they
sentences.zh: 看来诊所都在遵守法律，诊所不想承担他们

sentences.en: and their staffs could be sued maybe many times for the same act, that it's just too risky to take that chance.
sentences.zh: 和他们的员工可能因为同一行为而被起诉多次的风险，冒这个险实在太危险了。

sentences.en: Does that mean that they are, since September 1st, no longer providing abortions after six weeks in Texas?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着自9月1日以来，他们在德克萨斯州不再提供六周后的堕胎服务？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There are about 24 clinics in Texas.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯州大约有24家诊所。

sentences.en: And our reporting is suggesting that they have shut down their operations for post-six-week abortions.
sentences.zh: 我们的报道表明，他们已经停止了六周后堕胎的业务。

sentences.en: And six weeks is very early.
sentences.zh: 六周时间非常早。

sentences.en: It's before many women even though they're pregnant.
sentences.zh: 甚至在许多女性知道自己怀孕之前。

sentences.en: I mean, if you are opposed to abortion, this has to look like a very successful legal experiment,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你反对堕胎，这一定看起来像一个非常成功的法律实验，

sentences.en: and one that I imagine many conservative state lawmakers around the country would be eager to replicate.
sentences.zh: 而且我想全国许多保守派州议员都会渴望效仿。

sentences.en: Opponents of abortion are delighted with this law, and they will be copied in short order all over the parts of the country controlled by Republicans.
sentences.zh: 堕胎反对者对这项法律感到高兴，它将在不久的将来在全国所有由共和党控制的地区被复制。

sentences.en: Which increases the chance that the Supreme Court will have to contend with the question of whether or not this law is legal, whether it violates Roe v.
sentences.zh: 这增加了最高法院将不得不应对该法律是否合法、是否违反罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案这一问题的几率。

sentences.en: Maybe, or maybe the majority is right that this is an effective way to avoid judicial review.
sentences.zh: 也许吧，或者多数派是对的，即这是逃避司法审查的有效方法。

sentences.en: And let me broaden out your question in just one way, Michael.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，让我稍微扩大一下你的问题。

sentences.en: This is not the only area in which you could set up such a bounty system.
sentences.zh: 这并不是唯一一个你可以建立这种悬赏系统的领域。

sentences.en: A blue state could say, we understand the Second Amendment protects the right to own a gun in a home for self-defense,
sentences.zh: 一个蓝州可能会说，我们理解宪法第二修正案保护在家里拥有枪支用于自卫的权利，

sentences.en: but we're going to have a bounty system that allows any citizen of Massachusetts to sue people who have a gun in their home.
sentences.zh: 但我们将建立一个悬赏系统，允许马萨诸塞州的任何公民起诉在家里有枪的人。

sentences.en: And we'll give them $10,000 if they win.
sentences.zh: 如果他们赢了，我们将给他们一万美元。

sentences.en: Now, maybe they won't win, but we're going to have such a bounty system.
sentences.zh: 现在，也许他们不会赢，但我们将建立这样一个悬赏系统。

sentences.en: Would the Supreme Court go along with that?
sentences.zh: 最高法院会顺从这一点吗？

sentences.en: I, you know, I wonder.
sentences.zh: 我，你知道，我在想。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If we assume that at some point a case arises for the court that tests the core question of whether you can ban abortion under Roe v.
sentences.zh: 如果我们假设在某个时候，法院出现了一个案件，考验着你是否可以在罗诉

sentences.en: Wade, not who you can sue or who you can't sue, how should we think about who was in this majority in this case and whether those
sentences.zh: 韦德案下禁止堕胎的核心问题，而不是你可以起诉谁或你不可以起诉谁，我们该如何看待本案中多数派的组成，以及这

sentences.en: same five justices are likely to try to roll back Roe v.
sentences.zh: 同五位大法官是否可能试图推翻罗诉

sentences.en: Wade?
sentences.zh: 韦德案？

sentences.en: Is that the right way to think about this group of justices?
sentences.zh: 这是思考这群大法官的正确方式吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there's powerful evidence, not on the words of the decision, but in the posture of the decision and the novelty of the decision going along with this effort to evade
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为有强有力的证据表明，不是根据判决的字眼，而是根据判决的姿态以及与逃避宪法审查的努力相伴随的判决新颖性，

sentences.en: constitutional review, that the five justices in the majority are going to be also quite receptive to arguments that Roe itself should be overruled.
sentences.zh: 多数派中的五位大法官也将非常乐意接受应该推翻罗诉韦德案本身的论点。

sentences.en: But Adam, on a practical level, haven't these five conservative justices in a way just overturned Roe v.
sentences.zh: 但亚当，从实际层面来看，这五位保守派大法官难道不是在某种程度上刚刚推翻了德克萨斯州的罗诉

sentences.en: Wade in Texas?
sentences.zh: 韦德案吗？

sentences.en: On a practical level, I don't know that they've overturned it, but they have effectively eliminated the right to abortion announced in Roe v.
sentences.zh: 从实际层面来看，我不知道他们是否推翻了它，但他们实际上消除了罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案中所宣示的堕胎权。

sentences.en: They'll have a chance soon enough to address whether they want to overrule Roe v.
sentences.zh: 他们很快就会有机会阐明，他们是否希望在一桩本期法院审理单上的案件中，明确表示他们想要推翻罗诉

sentences.en: Wade in so many words in a case that's on the court's docket this term.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: And based on what we learned about the conservative majority in this case, there's good reason to think that Roe is engraved danger.
sentences.zh: 根据我们对本案中保守派多数派的了解，我们有充分的理由认为罗诉韦德案正处于严重危险之中。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The next major abortion case that the
sentences.zh: 最高法院预计将

sentences.en: Supreme Court is expected to rule on involves a Mississippi law banning the procedure after 15 weeks of pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 作出裁决的下一个重大堕胎案涉及密西西比州一项禁止怀孕15周后进行该手术的法律。

sentences.en: The justices will hear arguments in that case this fall.
sentences.zh: 大法官们将于今年秋天听取该案的辩论。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Three days after Hurricane Ida made landfall in Louisiana, it tore through the northeast, killing at least 43 people.
sentences.zh: 飓风“艾达”在路易斯安那州登陆三天后，席卷了东北部，造成至少43人死亡。

sentences.en: Much of the storm's destruction came from intense rain, which fell at a rate of three inches per hour, flooding roadways, subways, and entire neighborhoods.
sentences.zh: 这场风暴的大部分破坏来自强烈的降雨，降雨量达到每小时三英寸，淹没了道路、地铁和整个街区。

sentences.en: Many of those who died drowned in low-lying homes, basement apartments, and cars.
sentences.zh: 许多死者在低洼房屋、地下室公寓和汽车中溺水身亡。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Jessica Chung, Sidney Harper, Robert Jemison, and Lindsay Garrison.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由杰西卡·钟、西德尼·哈珀、罗伯特·杰米森和林赛·加里森制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Lisa Chow, contains original music by Dan Powell and Marian Lozano, and engineered by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由丽莎·乔伊编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔和玛丽安·洛扎诺的原创音乐，由丹·鲍威尔担任工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you on Tuesday after the holiday.
sentences.zh: 节假日后周二见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和萨拉·科尼格主持的《都会》最新一期节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 都会。

sentences.zh: 请在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
